open_points.subject: Project last-changed instant
open_points.text: Written once, derived and not a fact of its own: the last-changed instant
open_points.question: Is the project's last-changed instant a stored fact of the Project record (as 'Revisions and times' says: 'A record carries the instant it was created and the instant it was last changed') or a derived value, and how can it be 'written once' when the same section lists the actions that move it?
options: a stored fact, rewritten on every change that moves it
derived at read time from the revision history or audit log
stored, written once per revision (one instant per revision)
open_points.default_guess: a stored fact on the Project record, overwritten by each change that moves it; 'written once' is a slip

open_points.subject: Project revision — which actions move it
open_points.text: the project, status `archived`; nothing is deleted (V1-7); archiving an archived project returns it unchanged (R0-12)
open_points.question: Which actions move the project's revision: only 'correct a project', or also archiving, adding a room, publishing/withdrawing a pointer, anonymising? The texts list what moves the last-changed instant but R0-35 says 'every accepted change' moves the revision, and the archive action's output names no next revision.
options: only corrections of the card (name, alias, customer link, object)
corrections and archiving
every accepted change on the project, rooms and pointers included
open_points.default_guess: the revision moves exactly when the last-changed instant moves (card corrections and the one archiving)

open_points.subject: Customer revision — which actions move it and which must state one
open_points.text: the Customer with the new contact data, kind or fiscal data — tax id, legal name (R0-80) — next revision
open_points.question: Do restricting, lifting, ending, resuming and erasing move the Customer's revision, and must those actions state the revision they were made against (stale refused), or is the revision only for 'correct a customer'? The last-changed instant is said to move for all of them; the revision is not.
options: revision moves only on correction; marks need no stated revision
revision moves on every change including marks and erasure; every change states one
revision moves on every change but only corrections must state one
open_points.default_guess: the revision moves on every change of the Customer record, and only 'correct a customer' must state the revision it was made against

open_points.subject: What an anonymised project keeps
open_points.text: the project anonymised — its id, status and artifact pointers stay, its name, object and customer link go, `validate` answers `archived` — or deleted whole, `validate` answering `not_found`; the owner chooses (R0-60)
open_points.question: State 0 (R0-62) says an anonymised project keeps 'its id, status and artifact pointers and nothing else'; State 1 M01 settles that it also keeps the archived instant and the anonymised instant (and the anonymised mark). Which list is the model's?
options: id, status, pointers only (State 0)
id, status, pointers, archived instant, anonymised instant, anonymised mark (State 1)
open_points.default_guess: the State 1 list, recorded as a new owner decision narrowing R0-62

open_points.subject: Project deleted whole — remembered id
open_points.text: archived -> deleted whole     (owner, confirming; the record is gone, R0-60)
open_points.question: After a project is deleted whole, does Registry keep any trace of its `project_id` (so that an import conflict check or a later mint can never reuse it, and the audit entry's subject still resolves), or is the id simply gone with the record?
options: no trace; the id is gone
a tombstone of the id only (no personal value)
the audit entry is the only trace
open_points.default_guess: no separate tombstone; the audit entry naming the id is the only trace, and UUID minting makes reuse practically impossible

open_points.subject: Imported records — created/archived instants and acting principal
open_points.text: written once: the instant it was created; the instant it was archived
open_points.question: For a project, room or pointer brought in by the import, is the created instant (and for an archived project the archived instant; for a pointer the published/superseded instant) the v1 value from the export, or the instant of the import? And which acting principal (M07) does an imported room or pointer carry, since v1 recorded none?
options: v1 instants kept; principal recorded as 'owner' (the importer)
import instant everywhere; principal 'owner'
v1 instants kept; principal absent for imported records
open_points.default_guess: v1 instants kept where the export carries them, otherwise the import instant; the acting principal of every imported room and pointer is the owner

open_points.subject: Object kind — vocabulary
open_points.text: customer or object — address, kind, characteristics (R0-45) — next revision of the project
open_points.question: Is the object's kind a closed vocabulary the specification declares (like customer kind) or free text the owner writes? 'Declared vocabularies' does not list it, and whether kind is required at creation is not said.
options: a declared closed vocabulary (e.g. flat, house, building, commercial)
free text, owner-written, optional
open_points.default_guess: a declared closed vocabulary, optional at creation (only the address is required)

open_points.subject: Erasure and the other marks — settled or carried
open_points.text: marks stay independent facts; erasure clears none of them.
open_points.question: The Lifecycle candidate says what erasure does to the restricted and ended marks 'is settled in State 2 if anything', while Open questions says the owner settled on 2026-10-31 that erasure clears none of them. Which holds?
options: settled: erasure clears no mark
carried to State 2
open_points.default_guess: settled: erasure clears no mark; the lifecycle sentence is stale

open_points.subject: Marks after erasure
open_points.text: recorded -> erased                            final, owner (R0-06, R0-67)
open_points.question: Can the restricted and ended marks still be set, lifted or cleared on an erased Customer? State 0 refuses 'restrict or lift' and 'end or resume' on an erased customer, but the lifecycle shows the two mark pairs as orthogonal with no stop at erasure.
options: marks freeze at erasure (every change of them refused, as State 0 says)
marks stay toggleable after erasure
open_points.default_guess: marks freeze at erasure; the lifecycle should say so

open_points.subject: Erased Customer — does it keep its kind
open_points.text: An erased Customer is read as its `customer_ref`, its kind, the erased mark
open_points.question: State 0 says an erased Customer 'keeps only its identity and the fact that it was erased'; State 1 says it keeps its kind too (and the erased instant). Does the kind survive erasure?
options: kind kept (State 1)
kind gone with the rest (State 0)
open_points.default_guess: kind kept, as a business_confidential fact that identifies no one

open_points.subject: Erasure of contact data — does it erase fiscal data
open_points.text: name, phone, e-mail and language are gone; projects still name it (R0-06)
open_points.question: State 0's 'erase a customer's contact data' names only name, phone, e-mail and language as gone; State 1 M04 says tax id and legal name are gone too. Is there one erasure of all personal values, or a contact-data erasure that leaves fiscal data (which R0-80 added later) in place?
options: one erasure removes contact and fiscal data together (State 1)
contact-data erasure leaves fiscal data; a separate erasure or none for it (State 0 wording)
open_points.default_guess: one erasure removes every personal value of the Customer, fiscal data included

open_points.subject: Customer made by the import — kind and absent name
open_points.text: a v1 `customer_ref` that is not a Registry-minted id becomes a new Customer with a minted `customer_ref`, the old value moving to its tax id when it is one, and its projects are linked to that Customer (R0-80)
open_points.question: 'Record a customer' refuses a missing name or kind, yet the import creates a Customer with an absent name. Which kind does that Customer get (the v1 value does not say person or company), and is a Customer with no name a state the model allows in general or only for import-made ones?
options: kind inferred from the tax id form (CIF -> company, NIF/NIE -> person); absent name allowed only via import
owner gives kind (and name) at import time with the display names
a default kind (person); the owner corrects after
open_points.default_guess: the owner gives kind and name for each import-made Customer in the import itself, as it gives display names (R0-85)

open_points.subject: v1 customer_ref value that is not a tax id
open_points.text: the old value moving to its tax id when it is one
open_points.question: When the v1 `customer_ref` is neither a Registry-minted id nor a tax id, where does the old value go — dropped, kept as the Customer's name, kept as legal name, or does the import refuse it?
options: dropped; the owner records the data after
stored as the Customer's name
the import is refused for that project
open_points.default_guess: dropped; the new Customer starts with only a minted customer_ref and the import's audit entry

open_points.subject: Identity format — UUID or owner's choice
open_points.kind: contradiction (format left open vs ids kept)
open_points.text: the owner may choose otherwise, and the import then maps v1
open_points.question: State 0 (R0-50, R0-79) fixes that the import keeps the v1 ids verbatim ('under the ids Client Portal already names'); State 1 leaves the format open and allows a mapping. Is the format settled as UUID with ids kept verbatim, or is a different format with mapped ids still possible?
options: UUID, v1 ids kept verbatim (settled)
format open; import maps ids if the owner chooses another format
open_points.default_guess: UUID, ids kept verbatim; the 'may choose otherwise' clause is removed

open_points.subject: Telling a Registry-minted customer_ref from a v1 value
open_points.text: its identity `customer_ref`, minted by Registry (R0-16) or kept by the import
open_points.question: How does the import decide that a v1 `customer_ref` 'is a Registry-minted one' and keep it, versus a free value to replace: by UUID form alone, by the v1 export marking it, or by the owner's mapping? A v1 value that happens to be a UUID would otherwise be kept as if minted.
options: UUID form alone
the export marks which refs v1 minted
the owner's mapping decides per customer
open_points.default_guess: a v1 customer_ref that v1 itself minted (as the export marks it) is kept; everything else becomes a new Customer

open_points.subject: Access version — what moves it
open_points.text: None for identity. The access version's start and what moves it are State 2's
open_points.question: The Facts list states that the access version moves on every change of the granted set, the active project or the pending request; Open questions says what moves it is State 2's. Is the list of moving actions a State 1 fact or carried?
options: fact as listed (grant, revoke, active change, request made/cleared)
carried to State 2 entirely
open_points.default_guess: the listed actions move it and State 2 only fixes the start value and replay semantics

open_points.subject: Which actions produce an audit entry
open_points.text: change to a project or a customer record, a grant or revocation of a session's
open_points.question: Which product actions write an AuditEntry? Unclear: the import (M10 says 'the audit can name what was imported'), adding a room and publishing/withdrawing a pointer (changes to a project, or not since they do not move its last-changed instant), changing or clearing the active project, answering a request by declining, registering a session, ending/resuming a relationship, erasing a project whole.
options: only the R0-58 list read narrowly (card changes, grants/revocations, restriction, erasures, audit erasure)
every owner write and every agent write (rooms, pointers) too
R0-58 list plus import, active-project change and relationship end/resume
open_points.default_guess: every owner action that changes a record (import, active-project change, decline, end/resume included) and no agent write (rooms, pointers) or session registration

open_points.subject: Confirmation id — origin and record
open_points.text: the confirmation id where the owner confirmed (R0-37);
open_points.question: What is the confirmation id: who mints it (Registry at the confirmation step of the owner interface?), is it a fact of any model besides the AuditEntry and MigrationClosure that cite it, and does a confirmation leave a record of its own that the id resolves to?
options: Registry mints it per confirmed action; it lives only inside the audit entry
a separate Confirmation record with its own identity
the OwnerSession id plus an instant
open_points.default_guess: Registry mints an opaque id when the owner confirms; it is stored only in the audit entry (and MigrationClosure) and resolves to nothing else

open_points.subject: Class of the end-of-relationship date and restriction mark
open_points.text: the end-of-relationship date and the restriction mark where they are read together with a customer's name
open_points.question: Does a field have one disclosure class (R0-26 declares the class of each output) or does the ended date's class depend on what it is read with? The table lists the ended date and restriction mark as personal_data in one row and as business_confidential 'without its values' in another.
options: ended date and marks are business_confidential; an answer's class is the highest of its fields
ended date is personal_data always
class depends on the answer, as written
open_points.default_guess: each field has one class — ended date and marks business_confidential — and an answer takes the highest class of the fields it carries

open_points.subject: Unclassed facts — MigrationClosure and OwnerSession
open_points.text: every agent session fact; every audit entry
open_points.question: The table assigns no class to the MigrationClosure's facts (instant, confirmation id, file digest) or the OwnerSession's (identity, began, expiry). Which class do they carry when read (the import's refusal, the audit view)?
options: business_confidential
never returned, so no class needed
open_points.default_guess: business_confidential, owner only
